captions.text:
Microservices almost killed our team velocity. Here is why modular monoliths are quietly winning in 2026 🏗️

When you split a codebase before domain boundaries solidify, you don't get decoupling—you get distributed chaos.

Key takeaways:
1. Boundaries via module encapsulation
2. Single atomic deployment pipeline
3. Zero distributed tracing overhead

Are you scaling microservices or consolidating back?

The fastest distributed system is the one that isn't distributed.

3 reasons high-growth teams are returning to modular monoliths:
→ Instant local development setup
→ Zero eventual consistency bugs
→ Single repo refactoring speed

Build clear domain boundaries in code before building network boundaries between servers.

Stop typing 40-character bash commands every 5 minutes ⚡ 3 terminal upgrades that change developer workflow:

1. zoxide (cd on steroids)
2. fzf (instant fuzzy find)
3. lazygit (keyboard-only commits)

Comment 'TOOLS' and I'll send you my dotfiles config!

2. Use isolated feature buckets to decouple work streams.
3. Validate boundary states continuously.
